label: first copied-token input (recall_idx 1) in length-3 sequences
explanation: Active only in the copy phase of very short sequences, at the step right after <DEL> is consumed, where the input is the first original token fed back and the model must output original token 1 (t = L+1, recall_idx 1). L=3 holds about 87% of activation mass and essentially all of the strongest activations (top examples are all L=3, e.g. s q q <DEL> [s]). About 13% of mass comes from the same position in L=4 sequences, firing more weakly and only on some of them, with a token dependence (input s/u/b/f more often). A small tail is at recall_idx 2 (to_go 0 in L=3). It never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, at recall_idx 0, or for L >= 5. Within L=3 recall_idx 1 it is silent on about 20% of sequences, often when the first token is r/y/d/z/t, but excluding those tokens did not improve F1. Magnitude is largest for L=3 and depends on the token; I did not find a clean rule for the token part.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: s, u, b, f, x, 1; least: y, t, k, o) and the third original token (most: q, p, a, k, o, t; least: j, d, h, i); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, L=3, t=4.
